title: Microsoft Purview: protect data sent to unmanaged cloud apps through Palo Alto Prisma Access
summary: The briefing's default state, licensing requirements, roadmap targets and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should preserve the planned wording of the preview rollout, clarify abbreviated wizard paths and acknowledge conflicting Microsoft descriptions of billable requests.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview network data security now integrates with Palo Alto Prisma Access, extending discovery and protection to network traffic.

claims.quote: new and existing Palo Alto Prisma Access customers can configure Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention policies to discover and protect sensitive data

claims.where: Cost and licensing: definition of request
claims.claim: Learn defines a request as a device or browser network call to a website or API, excluding the response.
claims.quote: A request is each network call made from a device or browser to a website or API. This definition doesn't include the responses to the requests.
claims.fix: After the request definition, add: 'Microsoft's Azure pricing FAQ uses a different example, counting a generative AI prompt and its response as two requests; confirm the applicable billing definition before estimating spend.' Cite https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/#faq, which says 'a prompt is considered a request, as is a response from the AI app (2 total)'. Retain the Learn definition with its attribution.

claims.claim: The Purview billing models page states that network data security counts outbound requests only.
claims.quote: Network data security only counts requests that are outbound from the device.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go billing is Azure-based and requires the Microsoft 365 tenant to be associated with an active Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: An Azure bill for total pay-as-you-go charges across Microsoft solutions is generated at month end.
claims.quote: An Azure bill is generated at the end of the month for the total number of pay-as-you-go charges across all Microsoft solutions.

claims.claim: Billable volume depends on traffic in the scope of Purview policies rather than all Prisma Access traffic indiscriminately.
claims.quote: Customers will only be billed for requests that are detected within the scope of a Purview policy (e.g. collection policy, labeling policy, or DLP policy).
claims.fix: Add https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/ to sources and cite its 'Data Security | In Transit Protection' section for the sentence about request volume following policy-scoped traffic.

claims.claim: The billing models page links to Microsoft's pay-as-you-go pricing and cost estimator.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented automation for enabling the Purview DLP Security Store Prisma Access integration was found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Security Store Palo Alto Prisma Access enable integration API PowerShell collection policies New CollectionPolicy network automation', 'Purview Security Store API enable integration'; read network setup and Graph data security API overview; no enablement operation found.

claims.claim: The printed network DLP creation path follows the documented wizard route but omits app and group scoping steps.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. ... Select Inline web traffic. ... Select Custom ... Custom policy ... On the Choose where to enforce the policy page, ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is On
claims.fix: In front matter and the table, expand the path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > All unmanaged AI apps > Edit scope > Include only specific > + Add inclusions > Specific users and groups > group > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. This is the cited scenario's route; 'group' is the administrator's chosen target.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Network") creates a network-plane DLP policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>"). ... Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy creates the policy container; rule creation and Audit only or Block choices are separate.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies ... DLP policies contain DLP rules ... The last command creates the DLP rule with the name "Copilot Rule"

claims.claim: Some features used in the cited DLP scenario are in preview.
claims.quote: Some features used in this scenario are in preview.

claims.claim: The collection-policy route uses documented labels in order but abbreviates classifier, activity, app, group and content-capture choices.
claims.quote: Open the Data loss prevention solution and navigate to Classifiers > Collection policies. ... Select + Create policy. ... Select + Add condition and choose Content contains. ... Ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is enabled
claims.fix: Expand the path in front matter and the table to 'Data loss prevention > Classifiers > Collection policies > + Create policy > + Add condition > Content contains > Classifiers > Edit > Scope for classifiers > Exclude classifiers > + Exclude classifiers > Choose Classifiers > classifiers > + Add activities > activities > + Add data source > Unmanaged cloud apps > apps > Edit scope > Include only specific > Included > + Add inclusions > group > Don't capture content > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'. The lower-case classifiers, activities, apps and group are administrator-selected targets, not new labels.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented network-specific collection-policy automation configuration was found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'collection Network New-FeatureConfiguration', 'Purview collection Network ScenarioConfig'; read New-FeatureConfiguration, collection policy setup and Graph API overview. Generic collection-policy PowerShell exists; no Network-specific configuration was found.

claims.claim: Collection policies provide network discovery and monitoring without DLP enforcement.
claims.quote: collection policies for data discovery, data loss prevention policies for protection ... If you are using network data security for monitoring only via collection policies, the communication is asynchronous.

claims.claim: The integration and its Purview policies are tenant-level controls, with policies capable of targeting selected users.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure collection policies that apply to all or selected users within the tenant. ... Administrators can configure DLP policies that apply to all or selected users within the tenant.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/security-datasecurityandgovernance-overview to sources for the tenant-level policy scope. The integration's tenant context is also supported by MC1257999's tenant enablement prerequisite.

claims.claim: The collection-policy wizard configures classifiers, activities, apps and group scope.
claims.quote: Select Classifiers and then Edit. ... Select + Add activities. ... Select the Unmanaged cloud apps tab. ... Search for the US Sales group, select it, and select Add.

claims.claim: The documented scenarios enable Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers as the network enforcement or detection location.
claims.quote: On the Choose where to enforce the policy page, ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is On, then select Next.

claims.claim: The pilot Audit only DLP-rule instruction points to rows 2 and 3 although neither row documents configuring rule actions.
claims.quote: Start with a collection policy or an Audit only DLP rule scoped to a pilot group before using Block (rows 2 and 3). ... creates the policy container, not rules or Audit only/Block.
claims.fix: Replace '(rows 2 and 3)' in that checklist item with '(row 3 for collection-policy creation; Audit only/Block rule configuration is not shown in this table)'. The Audit only/Block instruction has no corresponding control row; row 2 documents policy-container creation only.
